<!-- pr-reviewer: a7a32e421c4eca96459da0015e720d71efc370a3 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

The wire contour of a meshed model now posts its circles and fillets as G2 / G3 arcs, read back from the facets within the model's chord tolerance, cut by the analytic wire contour of #3937, judged by the wire laws under that tolerance, with the polygon path kept byte for byte for a profile with no fitted arc. The fit is careful about what is and is not an arc (minimum chords, sagitta bound, fit tolerance, degenerate runs refused, split points dropped nearest-first) and the laws catch a 2 um mutation. The new tests pin the circle and the fillets in both posts (ISO and Sodick), and the undercut law of #3210 now runs only for a cut that states a taper, which is the right narrowing.

Review basis: `gh pr view 4019` + `gh pr diff 4019` + the linked issue #3215, checked against the laws in AGENTS.md. The diff touches no process file (no `Process change: yes` needed), no new dependency, no build.rs / .github / scripts / a `.cargo` directory / xtask, no `cfg(windows)` lines (no Windows-only readings needed), no snapshot PNG.

What looks good
- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/model_arcs.rs` — the fit is bounded by the model's own chord promise (not an absolute size): a true polygon (octagon, hexagon, a 63-facet mesh coarser than the bound) stays a polygon, a run of chords that bows past the bound is refused, and degenerate (too short, too few chords, or near-collinear) runs stay lines. The greedy walk starts after the longest edge so an arc is not split at the seam.
- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/model_tangent.rs` — the tangency nudge is applied only when the moved arc still holds every vertex of its run (`judge`), otherwise the fitted arc is kept, so a bad snap cannot silently bend the profile.
- `crates/app/src/operation/wire_verify.rs` — the facet-arcs cut is judged under the chord the fit was bounded by plus the fit's vertex tolerance (the generator's bound, read as the verifier reads it, plus `MODEL_ARC_FIT_TOL`), and the undercut law is skipped for the vertical cut (its absence is exactly the #3210 undercut law's scope).
- The pinning tests (11 in motion, 1 in sim, 4 in the app, one wire_verify assertion) cover both posts, the I/J centre increments, the kerf/cover law catch on a 2 um mutation, the refuses-by-name path, and the untouched polygon path.

Results merged with main
- Built on the self-hosted runner (Linux), PR #4019 head `a7a32e421c4eca96459da0015e720d71efc370a3`, trial-merged with main `138a592a196a6c68e8608b560fbd2696977a71c7`: [run 45643935556](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/45643935556) (conclusion: success). The run's own head check, collaborators-only check and read-only-PR refusal all passed; the trial merge was clean (the runner, not the reviewer, did it).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (the runner's gate summary, on the merged tree): 185 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled. Every wire suite is ok — `wire_4axis`, `wire_burnout`, `wire_contour`, `wire_dxf_selection`, `wire_post` (the new `model_arcs` submodule included), `wire_sharp_corners`, `wire_stamp`, `wire_tabs`, `wire_taper`, `wire_taper_angle`, `wire_taper_chord`, `wire_tool`, `wire_verify`, `wire_verify_tol`, `motion lib`, `sim lib`, `mcp_wire_contour` — plus the example catalog suites `example_catalog` (ok 24s), `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work` (ok).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` (runner): clean.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`, release, local worktree `cc-pr4019-review`, trial-merged with main `49bfcaea8`, -j 6): 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 15.9 min (`motion` lib and 4 `motion` suites + the `app` `pocket_pass_start` twin; log `gate-logs/light-20261125-161724`). Green on this head's merged tree. The author also ran it on the final head before the PR was flagged ready (`gates/3215-a7a32e421-light.log`), which is consistent.

Targeted tests
- The wire post/arc suites and the wire verification suites ran in the quick gate above (all ok), and the example catalog suites (`example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`) ran ok — the diff touches a post and a toolpath, and those are the suites it touches.
- Light lane: green, run by the reviewer on the trial-merged tree (6 steps, 0 failed). No `P1` under the safety floor: none is owed.
- No targeted heavy step: this is a P6 (not P1/P2) PR, and the author named the light lane in the PR body as its `cargo xtask gate light` run on this head; no P1 under the safety floor applies (the review-prs step says a P1 PR under the safety floor gets one targeted heavy step).

Requested before merge
1. (none blocking)

Questions / notes (not blocking)
- Issue #3215's "done means" asks for a full circle and a fillet "pinned by goldens". The PR pins both by tests that assert the posted arcs (centre, radius, I/J, line count, law verdict) rather than by a golden `.nc`; the wire goldens stay byte for byte as the PR body documents. If goldens on the arc path are expected this is a follow-up, not a blocker.
- The generator bounds the fit by `CHORD_CAP + material.excess` (the plain `material_of` read), while the verifier judges under `CHORD_CAP + judged_material(src, stock).excess + MODEL_ARC_FIT_TOL` (the stock's excess is folded in). The verifier's tolerance is therefore at least as wide as the generator's bound plus the vertex fit — a slightly wider tolerance, in the safe direction, not a wrong refusal. Consider reading one of them from the other for a single source of truth.
- `crates/app/src/operation/wire_op.rs` is 507 lines (was 506), i.e. over the ~400-line house rule; the PR acknowledges this and keeps the new logic in its own motion modules. A split of that file (the hook for its note) would let it stay under the line.
- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/model_arcs.rs` and the tests live in the `motion` crate, which is the lowest crate that provides them — good. `model_arcs_tests.rs` is a lib module inside it, not a new integration binary — good.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
